name: Chris Pinkham
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded South Africa's first commercial ISP, Internet Africa (Ticsa), which began offering internet access in November 1993 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Singapore to a military family, Chris Pinkham moved to South Africa at age 9 and grew up in Cape Town. He studied computer science at the University of Cape Town, where he worked at the computer data centre to fund his honours degree and was first exposed to the internet. He then spent about a year in Portland, Oregon working for Randy Bush, where he observed the emergence of ISPs in the US. Upon returning to South Africa in 1993, he co-founded the country's first commercial ISP with Paul Nash and Alan Barrett.

parent_family_domain_summary: Father was in the military; no evidence of parental domain expertise in technology or computing is documented in reviewed sources.

evidence_summary: Chris Pinkham's early advantage came from his exposure to internet technology at the University of Cape Town's computer data centre, where he worked to fund his honours degree after being unable to afford further study. His time in Portland working with Randy Bush gave him firsthand exposure to the emerging ISP industry in the US, which he brought back to South Africa. He co-founded Internet Africa with Paul Nash and Alan Barrett, leveraging his scarce networking expertise in a market with no existing ISPs. No specific family financial or domain advantages are documented in reviewed sources; his father was in the military.

current_position: Semi-retired; serves as independent director on the board of Jumo (Cape Town-based financial services company). Former VP Engineering at Twitter and founder/CEO of Nimbula (acquired by Oracle for $110M in 2013).
